name: news-20260814-auto-mode-stateless-mcp
title: Defaults That Stop Asking — Auto Mode and Stateless MCP
summary: Two changes from the same week in one piece — from 2026-08-14 Claude Code makes auto mode the default for new Pro, Max, and Team sessions (97% of prompts approved, people refused a planted dangerous command only 13.6% of the time, the classifier blocked 89%, and Trajectory Labs saw zero successes across 720 injection attempts), while the MCP 2026-07-28 spec deleted the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id to take state out of the protocol (_meta, server/discover, server-minted handles, Tasks/MCP Apps/enterprise authorization extensions, wire-incompatible both ways). The shared structure: remove the fixed point held at runtime and move the decision to declared rules and per-request data

name: wr-knowledge-vault
title: The Man Who Records Everything, and the Wiki That Publishes — Reflections on Knowledge Vaults
summary: Starting from the questions 'is this wiki RAG, an LLM wiki, or a second brain?', this reflection dissects the conversation transcript of a lifelogging practitioner who streams his entire life — 24-hour audio and screen capture — into a note vault, and compares his system with this wiki: the five-layer daily note (intent, execution, reality, interpretation, AI logs), the raw/wiki vault split and an ingest that asks back 'why did you keep this?' (motive as data), RAG vs LLM wiki as query-time vs keep-time tidying, the maxim that an ontology is a document rather than a graph, and the failure theory that purposeless hoarding breeds tombs of knowledge. It closes with four steps for this wiki: explicit capture motives, automated monthly retrospectives, a private inbox layer, and a conversational QA entry point

name: gdb-graphrag
title: Graph Databases & GraphRAG — Store the Relationships, Change the Answers
summary: An introductory explainer that chains graph databases to GraphRAG in one pass — property graphs that walk edges instead of computing JOINs and Cypher, the query language that looks like the drawing; GraphRAG stitching vector RAG's severed chunks back into a web so retrieval brings the whole neighborhood (multi-hop reasoning, preserved hierarchy, drawable evidence); ontology and graph schema as the web's blueprint (prerequisite relations in an education knowledge map); the similarly named stranger LangGraph (map of knowledge vs flowchart of work); domain cases from manufacturing failure logs to news categories; and a getting-started path from arrows.app sketches through Cypher export to turning a PDF into a knowledge graph with the neo4j-graphrag package (SimpleKGPipeline)

name: gdb-vector-retriever
title: Finding a Movie by Its Story — Your First Vector Retriever on a Neo4j Sandbox
summary: The hands-on companion to the concepts piece — borrow a graph DB in the browser with Neo4j Sandbox (the MovieLens-family Recommendations dataset: Movie, Genre, Actor, Director and User nodes, plus a RATED relationship that carries data), stroll the data with a few lines of Cypher, embed 100 movie plots into 1,536-dimensional vectors with an OpenAI embedding model and plant them as a plotEmbedding property, add a CREATE VECTOR INDEX (cosine similarity), then assemble a searcher with neo4j-graphrag's VectorRetriever (four parameters: driver, index, embedder, return properties). Summarise Toy Story's plot and the movie comes back in first place without its title ever being mentioned — the feel of vector search finding stories rather than words, and the next step toward GraphRAG: cast with vectors, walk with the graph

name: sks-im-not-ai
title: im-not-ai (Humanize KR) — An Editing Skill That Erases the AI Tell
summary: AI-written text gives itself away through habits, not grammar — an introduction to im-not-ai, an editing skill that finds and removes 33 traces such as inflated significance, aphorism formulas, signposting, fake candor, mechanical rule-of-three, and vague attribution. The body is blader's humanizer (MIT) vendored verbatim; its root is Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing". Covers the equally important false-positive half (judge by clusters of tells, preserve human signals, the author's sample outranks the rules, facts are immutable, respect the genre), the draft → two-question audit → final loop, installation and invocation, and this wiki's field record of passing all 121 indexed documents × 3 languages through it — only about 22 sentences of edits, with the style audit catching factual errors (7→9 views, a table summing wrong) along the way

relations.evidenceRef: The article delegates what a skill physically is (one markdown file in a folder) to 'What is a Skill' and builds the install/trigger explanation on top of it

name: tip-beginner
title: Beginner — 9 Habits That Save Context
summary: Nine starter tips for Claude Code, each checked against the official docs — /init to generate CLAUDE.md, the status line, keeping context small, hunting token hogs with /context, /compact vs /clear, plan mode (and what it means now that auto mode is the default), asking with problems not functions, the 95% ask-me-back prompt, and planting self-checks into to-dos

name: tip-intermediate
title: Intermediate — 11 Ways to Turn Sessions into a System
summary: Eleven tips for moving repetition into the system — parallel subagents (own context, summary-only reporting), building your own skills, running subagents on Haiku, updating CLAUDE.md with a 150–200 line cap, CLAUDE.md as a router, interrupting mid-run (Esc), pushing back then recording what works, /rewind checkpoints, hook notifications, image input, and screenshot-to-template

name: tip-advanced
title: Advanced — 8 Tips for Parallel, Autonomous, Scheduled Work
summary: Eight tips for parallel, autonomous, scheduled work, plus self-approval bias — collision-free parallel sessions with claude --worktree, calling APIs directly instead of MCP (context cost), the three tiers of scheduling (/loop, desktop tasks, cloud Routines), phone remote control, natural-language database queries, ultrathink and OMC's consensus-based ralplan, editing permissions in settings.json (auto mode's hard denies), and subagents vs agent teams (plus OMC's team mode). The rationale for splitting roles is self-preference bias — the ability to recognize one's own output correlates linearly with favoring it, and a single agent running plan→execute→verify turns that bias into a loop. Swapping models leaves conformity and echo chambers, so the answer has two layers: a planner→designer→verifier return path, and assigning the verifier to refute

name: gdb-onto-concepts
title: What Is an Ontology — Not a Warehouse of Data but a Map of Meaning
summary: The concept questions enterprise practitioners ask most, organized around an anonymized Korean webinar FAQ — a database is a warehouse storing values while an ontology is a map defining meaning, relations, and rules (Gruber's 'explicit specification of a conceptualization', W3C OWL 2); the four essential components (core concepts, relations, data, rules); the semantic layer as an interpreter between legacy (ERP·CRM·MES) and generative AI (not a migration; Palantir's 'digital twin of an organization' as precedent); why better LLMs still need ontologies (hallucination — OG-RAG's +55% fact recall, a clinical QA study cutting hallucination 63%→1.7%, an ontology query language constraining the LLM's degrees of freedom); and the graph DB as just one of three stores (RDB·vector·graph) an ontology orchestrates

relations.evidenceRef: Delegates knowledge graph / GraphRAG / 'fish with vectors, walk with graphs' concepts to the GraphRAG article and builds the ontology layer on top

name: gdb-onto-adoption
title: How Companies Adopt Ontologies — Cases · ROI · The Four-Step Build
summary: The practice part following the concepts — industry cases (finance's regulation-change tracing and claim adjudication, manufacturing's causal failure analysis, risk assessment and QMS quality tracing, SCM's inventory cause analysis) and the position as the stage before digital twins; ROI evolving from operating-cost savings to automation to restructuring revenue-linked work (plus the opportunity-cost view of decision speed and quality, traceable grounds); the four build steps of work selection, data selection, semantic structuring, and the verification cycle (success splits on systematizing verification — 'replace human limits with structure'); the three-track staffing of ontology engineer, IT, and domain experts with tool-drafted ontologies verified by experts; governance (terminology, KPIs, ownership, digitizing tacit knowledge) and the living ontology that stores executions and their evaluations; and a starting guide where the company that pays off its 'data debt' first pulls ahead

relations.evidenceRef: Delegates the definitions and principles of ontology and semantic layer to the concepts part and builds cases, ROI, and the build process on top
